findings.title: Persisted aggregate replay skips live cleanup reconciliation
findings.observation: When rollback-cleanup.json exists, executeRollbackWithCleanup immediately calls finalizePersistedRollback. That function completes lifecycle journals and writes terminal evidence from persisted observations but never invokes a live Docker reconciliation path.
findings.trigger: Persist a valid aggregate, interrupt before lifecycle or terminal completion, then let an exact attempt-owned production or restore resource reappear or drift before retry.
findings.impact: Retry can journal CLEANED and ROLLED_BACK or ROLLBACK_FAILED terminal authority while owned containers, networks or volumes still exist, giving operators and later lifecycle steps a false cleanup result.

evidence.description: A temporary exact-head aggregate-write crash regression recreated the exact restore container before retry. Retry resolved and terminalized without observing or deleting it; the container remained present. The temporary edit was removed and the feature diff returned clean.
The aggregate early return at lines 2695-2703 bypasses live cleanup paths, while finalizePersistedRollback at lines 2639-2667 only calls completeLifecycle and persistTerminalEvidence.
The design requires replay of completed cleanup to verify that current resources remain empty and to fail on conflicting content.
A fresh-context independent reviewer built a separate in-memory regression and independently reproduced the same stale ROLLED_BACK authority after restore-resource reappearance.

findings.remediation: Reuse durable application and cleanup results without repeating mutation, but actively reconcile every applicable PASS or preserved NOT_APPLICABLE live resource state before finalizing or replaying terminal authority. Reject nonempty or drifted state without deleting it or writing a success transition.
findings.verification: Add post-aggregate crash/retry regressions for restore reappearance, production reappearance and upgrade resource-set drift. Assert no second application rollback or deletion, require reconciliation failure, and prohibit successful lifecycle or terminal projection.
